rules.line: Hoard the work site before actual work starts. Keep all work inside the hoarded area. Follow Hoarding Details in Section 7 / 8.
rules.quote: The work site shall be hoarded up before actual work can commence on site. All works shall be confined within the hoarded area. The temporary hoarding shall comply with the details laid down in the “Hoarding Details” under Section 7.

rules.line: Make hoarding doors sliding, or make them open inward.
rules.quote: All hoarding doors installed shall either be sliding or open inward.

rules.line: Erect hoarding as per the PE-endorsed drawing and keep it structurally stable for the whole job (gypsum board at least 12 mm or metal sheet, secured with counterweights; inspect and maintain it).
rules.quote: The Applicant to ensure the hoarding is erected as per drawing endorsed by the PE and shall be responsible for the structural integrity and stability of the hoarding throughout the entire work period. This includes hoarding construction using approved materials, such as gypsum board with a minimum thickness of 12mm or metal sheet, properly secure and stabilized with suitable counterweights; regular check and necessary maintenance is carried out.

rules.line: Use non-combustible hoarding material (gypsum board). Submit the hoarding material and proof of non-combustibility in the CAG permit-to-work system.
rules.quote: Hoarding material used shall be of non-combustible material [i.e. Gypsum Board]. A copy of the hoarding material and its proof of its non-combustibility shall be submitted to CAG Permit to work system.

rules.line: Do not let hoarding block a fire protection system (for example fire curtains). If full-height hoarding is not feasible, cut an opening so the system still works, and use protective sheets to keep the outside clean.
rules.quote: The Applicant shall ensure that the hoarding does not obstruct any fire protection system (e.g. fire curtains). If a full height hoarding is not feasible, Applicant is required to create an opening in the hoarding to allow the normal functionality of the fire protection system.
